parcel_weights.name: Parcel dispatch
parcel_weights.feature: Ties and a sparse heavy tail; dropping heavy parcels changes the distribution.

issue_channels.name: Support requests
issue_channels.feature: Unequal channel counts; categorical eligibility changes the ranking.

repair_costs.name: Repair invoices
repair_costs.feature: Unequal group sizes and a Basic outlier separate count, mean and median.

material_samples.name: Material trial
material_samples.feature: Scrambled pairs distinguish independently sorted coordinates and wrong batch.

clinic_pairs.name: Clinic visits
clinic_pairs.feature: Missing plotting values require pairwise eligibility; a missing unrelated note must survive.

bike_routes.name: Bicycle routes
bike_routes.feature: Matched distances with systematically different times; derived speeds differ from raw duration.

bench_readings.name: Test bench readings
bench_readings.feature: Repeated readings are distinct observations, not one mean.

packing_runs.name: Packaging runs
packing_runs.feature: Numeric identifiers must be excluded from scientific correlation.

sound_sensors.name: Sound sensor checks
sound_sensors.feature: Invalid records create extremes and must be omitted from both views.

capacity_test.name: Service capacity test
capacity_test.feature: Chosen x benchmark 60 differs from median load 52.5.

particle_diameters.name: Particle measurements
particle_diameters.feature: Separated clusters allow a controlled smoothing comparison without changing rows.

delivery_delays.name: Delivery delays
delivery_delays.feature: Ties at five distinguish strictly above from at or above; zero is observed.

part_strength.name: Manufactured part strength
part_strength.feature: Equal centres but unequal spreads distinguish centre from interval meaning.

ceramic_checks.name: Ceramic checks
ceramic_checks.feature: Two values per group; an unrelated paired view must remain intact during repair.

machine_replicates.name: Machine replicates
machine_replicates.feature: Individual trajectories differ from mean and spread at repeated hours.

calibration_checks.name: Calibration checks
calibration_checks.feature: A documented failed calibration changes the full-table fit materially.

curved_response.name: Response experiment
curved_response.feature: Symmetric curved response creates structured nonzero straight-line residuals.

loading_waits.name: Loading-zone waits
loading_waits.feature: Measured zero, repeated cells and absent combinations have different meanings.

installations.name: Installation outputs
installations.feature: Global maximum is inactive; active maximum is a different paired record.

recycling_sites.name: Material collection
recycling_sites.feature: Unequal bases make stacked glass and zero-baseline glass comparisons different.

plant_trays.name: Plant-tray observations
plant_trays.feature: Three varying measurements, two groups and a numeric identifier.

reservoir_flow.name: Reservoir monitoring
reservoir_flow.feature: Overlapping measurement ranges need comparable relationship facets.

support_totals.name: Support team shifts
support_totals.feature: Unequal workloads make mean shift percentages differ from pooled resolution rates.

library_weeks.name: Library visits
library_weeks.feature: One observation per ordered week asks about change through time.

rainfall_log.name: Rainfall log
rainfall_log.feature: Dry days are known zero measurements; a rug retains repeated zeros.

sales_receipts.name: Shop receipts
sales_receipts.feature: Zero-unit rows are outside sold-item population; revenue is price times quantity.

weather_medians.name: Weather stations
weather_medians.feature: Asymmetric group values distinguish mean from median; repeated humidity exposes overlap.

river_replicates.name: River monitoring
river_replicates.feature: Unequal daily observation counts and changing spreads require within-time summaries, not a station trajectory.

cycle_commutes.name: Cycle commutes
cycle_commutes.feature: Paired distance and travel time have physical units; labels must identify the actual measurements.

bird_surveys.name: Bird surveys
bird_surveys.feature: Both habitats span several areas, making a colour mapping useful while an unrelated size mapping adds no new measurement.
bird_surveys.observationUnit: one survey of a measured area

stone_sizes.name: Stone measurements
stone_sizes.feature: Ties and a single large stone expose how bin resolution changes counts without changing evidence.

page_latencies.name: Page response checks
page_latencies.feature: A small right-skewed sample makes smoothing assumptions visible; its apparent tail cannot establish a population tail.

battery_trials.name: Battery trials
battery_trials.feature: Tied endurance values distinguish the at-or-below proportion from a strictly-above proportion.

soil_readings.name: Soil conductivity checks
soil_readings.feature: The repeated 1.4 readings remain two observations even when rug ticks coincide.

book_returns.name: Book returns
book_returns.feature: Shelf frequencies answer a workload question; days late are measurements and must not become bar heights.

bus_fares.name: Bus fare receipts
bus_fares.feature: An unusually costly Local ticket and unequal route counts separate mean, median and record count.

beam_loads.name: Beam load tests
beam_loads.feature: Materials A and B have equal means but different spreads; asymmetric C readings also distinguish mean from median.

circuit_lifetimes.name: Circuit lifetime tests
circuit_lifetimes.feature: A legitimate extreme in design A tests whether boxes retain flagged observations; small groups still limit quartile stability.

worm_lengths.name: Worm measurements
worm_lengths.feature: Three worms per habitat can demonstrate a violin call but cannot support dependable density or tail claims.

sensor_offsets.name: Sensor repeat checks
sensor_offsets.feature: Repeated equal offsets expose the difference between random category-direction jitter and exact category positions.

bolt_lengths.name: Bolt measurements
bolt_lengths.feature: Triplicate equal lengths require deterministic packing; removing duplicate values would remove real bolts.

ink_trials.name: Ink flow trials
ink_trials.feature: Only three trials per ink make the supplied detailed density draft unsuitable; duplicates must survive its replacement.

air_chambers.name: Air chamber tests
air_chambers.feature: Scrambled volumes and pressures catch independently sorted coordinates; these are measured associations, not causal evidence.

observatory_frames.name: Observatory exposures
observatory_frames.feature: Instrument identity benefits from redundant colour and shape; active collecting area varies within each instrument and is a separate third measurement.

glass_calibration.name: Glass calibration checks
glass_calibration.feature: The two batches have different offsets, so a batch-specific fitting question must not silently fit pooled records.

spring_response.name: Spring response tests
spring_response.feature: The supplied curved response creates residual structure; original extension values are not residuals.

greenhouse_checks.name: Greenhouse measurements
greenhouse_checks.feature: Three measured fields support pairwise comparisons; sample_id is a numeric identity and must be excluded.

museum_entries.name: Museum entries
museum_entries.feature: Door-by-ticket cells count people; an unobserved combination in a count matrix means zero records.

water_lab.name: Water laboratory checks
water_lab.feature: A distribution of pH and paired pH/conductivity view answer different questions using the same six samples.

production_checks.name: Production line checks
production_checks.feature: Pairs overlap across lines, so complete legends, redundant shapes and transparency support group recognition without altering measurements.

centrifuge_checks.name: Centrifuge checks
centrifuge_checks.feature: Mean and median yield differ; reference-line orientation must follow the benchmark measurement, not the other axis.

solar_checks.name: Solar panel checks
solar_checks.feature: The highest-output and smallest-area records differ; an annotation must use both coordinates from the selected row.

food_deliveries.name: Food delivery receipts
food_deliveries.feature: Depots have different totals and per-delivery means; prepared bar heights do not aggregate themselves.

lake_samples.name: Lake chemistry samples
lake_samples.feature: Three physical measurements and a numeric sample identity require deliberate variable selection before pairwise panels.

station_arrivals.name: Station arrival checks
station_arrivals.feature: The paired delay/passenger question and each measurement’s marginal distribution belong to different Axes on one grid-owned Figure.

coating_checks.name: Coating process checks
coating_checks.feature: Workshops have distinct thickness ranges; a relationship facet and a category-distribution facet answer separate questions.

report_checks.name: Report measurements
report_checks.feature: An already prepared chart isolates export responsibility; changing its evidence would not repair layout or produce a finished handoff.

travel_costs.name: Travel expense receipts
travel_costs.feature: Unequal category means expose misleading bar baselines and nonlinear length comparisons; the values must survive the axis repair.

harbour_trips.name: Harbour trip log
harbour_trips.feature: The longest distance belongs to a short trip outside the stated report; one duration selection must govern all three views.

teaching.title: Take a repeatable random sample
teaching.idea: head and tail take rows from the ends of a table. sample chooses rows from anywhere; random_state fixes the selection so a later run can reproduce it.
teaching.example: From four named rows, this two-row sample selects D and C. Running it again with the same seed selects the same rows.

import pandas as pd

sample.sample(n=2, random_state=1)

teaching.title: Two notations for an ordinary column
teaching.idea: Bracket selection is the general way to read a column. Attribute selection is a shortcut for simple column names that do not collide with DataFrame properties or methods.
teaching.example: For a column named reading, sample["reading"] and sample.reading select the same Series. A name such as "reading value" needs brackets.
teaching.code:
import pandas as pd

sample = pd.DataFrame({"reading": [2, 4]})
sample["reading"]

output.caption: Both notations select the reading column

teaching.noteTitle: Prefer brackets when names might conflict
teaching.note: Names such as index, columns and count already belong to pandas. Brackets avoid those collisions and work reliably with arbitrary field names.

teaching.title: Turn dtype objects into readable text
teaching.idea: df.dtypes returns a Series indexed by field names. Its values describe storage types. astype(str) converts those values to display text without changing the source table.
teaching.example: A numeric column has dtype int64. Converting the dtype Series to text produces the string "int64", not a conversion of the numeric column itself.
teaching.code:
import pandas as pd

sample = pd.DataFrame({"reading": [2, 4]})
types = sample.dtypes.astype(str)
pd.DataFrame({"dtype": types, "missing": sample.isna().sum()})

teaching.title: Meet np.select
teaching.idea: np.where chooses between two results. np.select handles several conditions: it checks them in order and uses the result for the first True condition.
teaching.example: A price of 6 matches both > 5 and > 3, so the > 5 condition must come first to label it high.
teaching.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

sample = pd.DataFrame({"price": [2, 4, 6]})
sample["band"] = np.select(
    [sample["price"] > 5, sample["price"] > 3],
    ["high", "middle"], default="low"
)
sample
parts: Choose one result for each row from several possible conditions.
Test these conditions in order; the first True one wins.
Pair each condition with its output label in the same position.
Use low when neither condition is True.
Store the chosen label beside each input price.
teaching.note: The price 6 satisfies both tests. If > 3 came first, 6 would be labelled middle before the > 5 test was reached.

teaching.title: Order counts by their labels
teaching.idea: value_counts counts each month but usually orders by frequency. sort_index reorders the resulting Series by month label, so the calendar runs from earlier to later months.
teaching.example: Month 3 appears twice and month 1 once. Sorting by index displays month 1 before month 3.
teaching.code:
import pandas as pd

sample = pd.Series([3, 1, 3], name="month")
sample.value_counts().sort_index()
parts: Count how many rows have each month number.
Sort the month labels on the left, not the count values on the right.
teaching.note: sort_values would rank months by how often they occurred. The report asks for calendar order, so sort the month index.

alternativeTeaching.title: Another way to draw this
alternativeTeaching.idea: sns.histplot reads named columns from data. Matplotlib ax.hist instead accepts the numeric observations directly; bins controls the same grouping into count bars.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

teaching.title: Build the category order from a grouped Series
teaching.idea: groupby and median produce one labelled value per bench. sort_values orders those medians while keeping each bench name attached; .index then supplies the ordered category names to order.
teaching.example: Ash=10, Birch=4 and Cedar=7 give category order Birch, Cedar, Ash. The chart still draws every raw reading; only its category positions use this summary.
teaching.code:
import pandas as pd

sample = pd.DataFrame({"bench": ["Ash", "Birch", "Cedar"], "reading": [10, 4, 7]})
medians = sample.groupby("bench")["reading"].median()
ranked = medians.sort_values()
order = ranked.index
list(order)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

Make two horizontal panels with batch order A, B, C and a common strength range 0 to 20. Left: mean strength with one-standard-deviation intervals and capsize=0.15, titled Mean and SD. Right: every raw strength value with jitter=False, titled Observations. Label batch and strength on both.
exercise.solution:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
sns.pointplot(
    data=df,
    x="batch",
    y="strength",
    order=["A", "B", "C"],
    estimator="mean",
    errorbar="sd",
    capsize=0.15,
    ax=axes[0],
)
axes[0].set_ylim(0, 20)
sns.stripplot(
    data=df, x="batch", y="strength", order=["A", "B", "C"], jitter=False, ax=axes[1]
)
axes[1].set_ylim(0, 20)
axes[0].set(title="Mean and SD", xlabel="batch", ylabel="strength")
axes[1].set(title="Observations", xlabel="batch", ylabel="strength")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Supplied setup — editable
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "bench": ["A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B", "C", "C"],
    "reading": [4, 4, 7, 2, 5, 5, 6, 8],
    "sequence": [1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2],
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import seaborn as sns

# Your work
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
medians = df.groupby("bench")["reading"].median()
ranked = medians.sort_values()
order = ranked.index
sns.swarmplot(data=df, x="bench", y="reading", order=order, size=5, ax=ax)
ax.set(title="Test bench readings", xlabel="bench", ylabel="reading")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import pandas as pd

data = {
    "zone": ["A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "C"],
    "side": ["Front", "Front", "Rear", "Rear", "Rear", "Front"],
    "wait_minutes": [0, 2, 4, 8, 10, 0],
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import seaborn as sns

# Your work
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
working = df.copy()
working["zero_wait"] = working["wait_minutes"] == 0
matrix = working.pivot_table(
    index="side", columns="zone", values="zero_wait", aggfunc="mean"
)
sns.heatmap(matrix, annot=True, fmt=".2f", cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1, ax=ax)
ax.set(title="Loading-zone waits", xlabel="zone", ylabel="side")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

exercise.task: Does the question concern composition, exact component comparisons or within-item shares? Each row is one item’s channel counts. Use the rows specified below from df. Compare Online and Shop shares within each item rather than their absolute counts. Draw 100% stacked bars in table item order: Online at the base, Shop above. Calculate each share using that item’s combined count, include a component legend and use a 0–100 percentage axis. Chart: title "Pet supplies sold"; x "item"; y "Share (%)".
exercise.solution:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
total = df["Online"] + df["Shop"]
online = df["Online"] / total * 100
shop = df["Shop"] / total * 100
ax.bar(df["item"], online, label="Online")
ax.bar(df["item"], shop, bottom=online, label="Shop")
ax.legend()
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax.set(title="Pet supplies sold", xlabel="item", ylabel="Share (%)")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
